summary: Boundary Bald Mountain, Somerset Co., ME: station 1911, 12 ft wood tower, 35 ft steel tower 1937 that collapsed 1971-76; a 2021 article describes remains on the summit.

facts.design: Three structures per Maine listing: station (1911), 12 ft wood tower (1914), 35 ft steel tower (1937)
facts.status_note: Tower collapsed between 1971 and 1976; the register says it was removed, but a 2021 Press Herald article describes the remains lying on the summit

access.note: Summit is on private timberland; a 2021 Press Herald article describes the logging road as open to the public and the old fire warden's trail as unmaintained

events.note: Lookout station built on Bald Mountain; a long-distance telephone line ran through Heald Pond Camps
Trail cut to the summit and a cellar made for the camp
12-foot wood tower per the Maine listing
Telephone box installed in the tower
Steel tower listed at 35 feet (the unit is not written in the listing; feet assumed)
Collapsed between 1971 and 1976; the 2021 article ties the collapse to the 1937 tower
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register, September 15, 2008

corrections.why: 3.7 m (12 ft) matches the 1914 wood tower in the Maine listing, not the 1937 steel tower listed at 35 ft that the 2021 article ties to the collapse. The listing gives 35 without a unit; feet assumed.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 2021 Press Herald article describes a log fire tower on the peak in the early 1900s; the Maine listing dates the first structure to 1911 and a wood tower to 1914; the lookout-history site gives a 1920 inventory of a 12-foot wood tower. The story reports 1911 as the first lookout station.
The register says the tower was removed; the 2021 Press Herald article says the remains of the fire tower lie in a rusted heap on the summit. The story reports both.

sources.title: Hiking in Maine: Close to Quebec, Boundary Bald Mountain provides a plethora of peaks

notes_for_editor: Brief height 3.7 m corresponds to the 1914 12-ft wood tower; the collapsed tower was the 1937 steel tower (35 as listed, unit inferred as feet). The summit's current state rests on a single 2021 article; the register and the article disagree on removal. Access is inferred from the article's description of the road and trail. No staffing or fire records found. No photos added.
